clocks.label: VENEZUELA TEXT
clocks.why: Caracas said a signing session was scheduled. This clock prices GEO-022, cut to 36% today: if it passes with no published contract - no governing law, no arbitration seat, no named sanctions authorisation - a 100-year concession exists only as a briefing. Today's reporting that senior US officials lobbied Swiss authorities over the money-laundering case against the venture's designated operator, under the line no Betancourt no energy-security deal, says the deal is being built around a PERSON rather than around infrastructure.

clocks.label: ENVOY WINDOW
clocks.why: Our own dated falsifier on GEO-005, now 17%. Witkoff and Kushner are reported to fly to Moscow and Kyiv this weekend, the first dated meeting since February. If no US envoy has landed in either capital by this date, the two points bought today come straight back off and GEO-005 returns to 14%.

clocks.label: BOJ DECISION
clocks.why: The Bank of Japan's policy meeting, and the clock behind GEO-025 at 28%. Japan is where the world borrows cheaply; the ten-year JGB is already near 3 per cent, the highest since 1996. A hike plus the yen through 150 is the confirmation leg - a rate decision in Tokyo transmitted as a margin call everywhere the cheap yen was spent.

clocks.label: HORMUZ FALSIFIER
clocks.why: Our own dated falsifier, published in advance so it can be scored against us. If no laden tanker is attacked inside the international lanes through this date AND Muscat publishes a minesweeping calendar or corridor coordinates, the recurrence read is a MISS: GEO-001 goes back toward 21 and GEO-003 back to about 31.

clocks.label: XI SUMMIT
clocks.why: The state visit GEO-006 at 87% and GEO-012 at 31% both hang on, and the date Washington wants its overcapacity finding published before. Brent's band question resolves the same day and is our first Brier score - raised to 35% today on geometry alone, with Brent around $96 and the $100 barrier four per cent away with twenty days left.

clocks.label: DIESEL BAN EXPIRY
clocks.why: Russia's ban on diesel exports, imposed after Ukrainian drones hit its refineries, runs to this date - one of three simultaneous pulls on world distillate that put US diesel at a record $5.820 a gallon. If the ban lapses and the crack does not fall, the strait was the binding constraint; if it lapses and the crack breaks, Russia was. The Kharg falsifier shares this date: loading terminals intact on 1 October scores the free-coercion read confirmed.

speculation.obs: Transit counting through Bab al-Mandab is contradicting the headline. As published by Lloyd's List Intelligence from Joint Maritime Information Center data, movements through the Red Sea's southern chokepoint reached at least 302 transits between 17 and 23 August - the highest level since the Saudi ban - driven by bulk carriers, product tankers and containerships, with JMIC assessing that the perceived Houthi threat is confined to a specific subset of Saudi-linked tonnage rather than to shipping generally.
speculation.src: Lloyd's List Intelligence Red Sea Brief, reporting Joint Maritime Information Center transit data
speculation.read: Labelled inference. This is the observation that argues AGAINST the day's loudest story, which is why it goes first. A ground offensive toward Mokha and 129 dead reads like a closing gate; the transit series says charterers are still sailing, because the war-risk desk has priced this as a quarrel with Riyadh rather than a threat to trade. If that holds, the Houthis have found something more useful than a closure - a blockade that costs one country and leaves the rest of the world with no reason to intervene. It is also the fragile part of the arrangement: discrimination this precise depends on target identification that has already failed at least once in every previous Red Sea campaign.
speculation.falsifier: A laden hull with no Saudi charter, owner or cargo link struck inside the international lanes, or a JMIC weekly transit count falling well below the 302 figure. Either would mean the discriminating read is dead and the market is repricing the strait itself.

speculation.obs: Tanker tracking shows the volume that moved onto the route now under attack. Kpler-derived figures reported by Middle East Eye put barrels through Bab al-Mandab up roughly eightfold since the Strait of Hormuz closed in March, as Saudi Arabia pushed crude across the East-West pipeline to Yanbu; maritime data also records at least 29 Saudi-linked vessels diverting away from the strait in the first two weeks of the declared blockade, and the attack on the tanker NCC Wafaa off Yanbu is described as the northernmost Houthi strike since the blockade began.
speculation.src: Kpler tracking data and maritime traffic records, as reported by Middle East Eye
speculation.read: Labelled inference, and the species is CONCENTRATION RISK made visible by transponders. The eightfold figure is the whole strategic picture in one number: the workaround built to escape one chokepoint delivered Saudi exports into the reach of the actor best equipped to charge for the second. The northward creep matters more than the tonnage - a strike off Yanbu is 700 nautical miles from Bab al-Mandab and puts the loading terminal, not just the transit, inside the threatened set. That is the difference between taxing a route and threatening a wellhead's only remaining door.
speculation.falsifier: Kpler or Vortexa volumes through the strait falling back toward pre-March levels without a corresponding rise in Saudi floating storage, which would mean the barrels found a third route rather than being deterred. A second attack north of Jeddah would confirm the creep instead.

speculation.obs: Two European central banks have quietly repositioned gold away from New York. De Nederlandsche Bank confirmed moving 86.4 tonnes out of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York and Ottawa to London between March and August, citing increasing geopolitical unrest and crisis readiness, lifting its London share from 18.1 to 32.1 per cent - but only about 27 tonnes physically travelled, the remainder executed as a sale of New York metal and a purchase of London bullion. The Banque de France replaced 129 tonnes held at the New York Fed between July 2025 and January 2026.
speculation.src: De Nederlandsche Bank statement, reported by Bloomberg, CNBC and Euronews
speculation.read: Labelled inference, and the mechanics are the analysis. A physical convoy would be a statement about counterparty trust; a book trade is a statement about SETTLEMENT LOCATION - you cannot sell metal into a market from a vault you believe cannot deliver. So the reading is not that Amsterdam distrusts the New York Fed, it is that both banks now want their reserves sitting where they can be mobilised into a crisis at London clearing speed rather than across an ocean and a time zone. The genuinely new fact underneath the noise is smaller and more durable than the conspiracy version: vault jurisdiction has become a variable European reserve managers actively manage, and it was not one five years ago.
speculation.falsifier: A third and fourth European central bank announcing the same move, or any of them requesting physical delivery materially in excess of the book entry, would push this from housekeeping toward a genuine counterparty judgement. A quiet reversal of the London share would kill it.

dossiers.name: Iran

glance.government: Islamic Republic - a clerical-military hybrid in which the security institutions have been ascendant since the February-May war
glance.leader: Mojtaba Khamenei, Supreme Leader since 8 Mar 2026, not verifiably seen in public for roughly six months; Masoud Pezeshkian president; IRGC commander-in-chief Ahmad Vahidi the operative center
glance.gdp: Roughly $300-390bn nominal depending on source; forecast to contract about 5% in 2026 with inflation near 70% and the rial at a record 2.02m to the dollar
glance.military: About 570,000-610,000 active (IISS puts it near 570,000) plus roughly 350,000 reserves; the IRGC Navy, not the regular navy, holds the strait
glance.influence: Transit rights and mine inventory at Hormuz, anti-ship missiles, Iraqi and Yemeni networks - set against oil revenue the central bank governor himself describes as having fallen to zero

dossiers.summary: Start with the constraint, not the man. Iran is a state whose one convertible asset - the barrel - has stopped moving, which is why its remaining leverage is geographic rather than economic, and why it is spent in advertised doses rather than banked. The desk that decides is the IRGC Navy and the new wartime security committee, not the presidency and not the invisible Leader: Washington routed its own peace offer through career Guard commanders, and Iran's president has said on state television that communicating with Khamenei is very difficult. That produces exactly the behaviour this board keeps recording - a volley at forewarned bases in Jordan that was almost entirely intercepted, mines laid and lanes conditionally cleared, six near-breakthroughs that each end in a restated condition. Prospect theory says a cornered regime gambles, but a regime whose survival runs through an institution that profits from the crisis has an interest in holding the temperature where it can still choose it. The falsifier is a strike that actually kills Americans, or a verified minesweeping calendar with published coordinates - either would show the temperature is no longer being chosen.

concerns: Mine and anti-ship capability at Hormuz is intact and reversible - a cleared lane is a maintenance schedule, not a settlement
Succession is unresolved in practice: an unseen Leader plus an IRGC that answers Washington's messages is a leadership fiction with a real chain of command underneath
Oil revenue near zero against 70% inflation removes the economic off-ramp that would normally price restraint
Escalation is now probabilistic rather than intentional - interception rates, not decisions, separate a message from a casualty event

Retaliation has gone HORIZONTAL: fire into US facilities in Jordan, Bahrain and Kuwait in a single night widens the number of surfaces on which the interception equilibrium can fail, and converts Gulf hosts from venues into potential parties

dossiers.name: Russia

glance.government: Presidential autocracy with a managed legislature; State Duma elections due September 2026
glance.leader: Vladimir Putin - the only decider on the war file; Peskov is a thermostat, not an actor
glance.population: About 144 million (2026 estimate; occupied-territory counting disputed)
glance.gdp: Roughly $2.7tn nominal; the government cut its 2026 growth forecast toward 0.4-1%, with oil and gas revenue reported down more than 25%
glance.military: About 1.3 million active with roughly 2 million reserves; defence spending near 6.3-6.5% of GDP
glance.influence: Sanctioned-barrel logistics including the Arctic route, Africa Corps guarantees in the Sahel, energy leverage over Europe, veto and nuclear status

dossiers.summary: Moscow's constraint is refining and money, not morale. Ukrainian deep strikes have pushed refinery runs to about 3.6m barrels a day, the lowest since 2002, and the fuel export ban first imposed in July is being weighed for a second extension - each extension a public admission of how much capacity is offline. The deciding desks are the defence and finance ministries rather than the foreign ministry: the September Duma election and the 6.3-6.5% of GDP the war costs are what price the negotiating posture, which is why the deep pause Peskov announced reads as a bargaining position taken from a front that is still moving at Pokrovsk. Watch where the state chose to spend a scarce asset this weekend - Africa Corps, roughly 200-300 personnel supplied overland through Burkina Faso, was used to save a junta in Niamey, buying an advertisement and incurring an obligation in the same act. The observables that would move this file are not statements but airlift and diesel: Flight Unit 224 traffic above its six-flight run rate, or refinery runs recovering past 4m barrels a day.

concerns: The fuel and refining constraint is the real bind - denial is working where punishment has not, and Kyiv is aiming at exactly that
The announced campaign against Ukraine's grid is punishment by Pape's definition, with a poor historical conversion into concessions
Sahel guarantees now carry a defend-the-palace obligation a 200-300 person detachment cannot scale
September Duma elections and a possible post-election reserve call-up are the domestic clock every diplomatic signal is priced against

The covert front against the supplier coalition is now formally attributed: Berlin blames Moscow for an explosive drone at Leipzig/Halle and closes the Bonn consulate on Sept 18, with the EU calling it state-sponsored terrorism - salami tactics against logistics rather than against forces

dossiers.name: Ukraine

glance.government: Wartime presidential republic under martial law; national elections suspended for the duration
glance.leader: Volodymyr Zelenskyy, constrained by coalition dependence; Rustem Umerov holds both the negotiating brief and the intelligence file
glance.population: About 39.5 million on mid-2026 estimates - wartime displacement makes every figure soft
glance.gdp: Roughly $225bn nominal (2025); the EU agreed a package of about EUR 90bn for 2026-27, funded by market borrowing rather than by seizing the roughly EUR 210bn of frozen Russian assets
glance.military: About 677,000 active on the IISS count; larger figures circulate and are not verified
glance.influence: A deep-strike drone campaign that has taken Russian refining to a 24-year low, the Black Sea corridor, and the political weight of being the coalition's test case

dossiers.summary: Kyiv's constraint is arithmetic - manpower, interceptors and a donor calendar - and it sets the strategy rather than following from it. The one instrument Ukraine owns outright is the drone campaign against Russian refineries, which is denial in Pape's sense and is measurably working; nearly everything else is rented from capitals that vote. That dependence is why the deciding desk is now split between the general staff and a negotiating channel run through Washington, and why Zelenskyy has to say yes to the joint Western plan and no to surrender in the same breath. It also explains Myla: an army under sustained deep strike disperses munitions into settlements, which lowers the odds of losing a depot and raises the odds of a night like Friday's, when 38 people died mostly from what the warehouse contained. The falsifiable claim for the winter is that Russia's fuel constraint shapes Russian behaviour more than blackouts shape Ukrainian negotiating positions - if Kyiv's position visibly softens under grid attack while Moscow's does not under fuel shortage, the model is wrong and we say so.

concerns: The announced Russian campaign against the electricity grid arrives with winter and with air-defence stocks already rationed
Pokrovsk is the axis Moscow names when it explains why it is in no hurry to talk; its fall would be a step change, not a line move
Funding is market-borrowed rather than asset-backed, which puts the money on a European political calendar
Dispersal of munitions into inhabited areas makes mass-casualty events recurrent regardless of anyone's aimpoint

dossiers.name: China

glance.government: Party-state under the most centralized leadership since Mao; a recent command purge reshaped the military timetable
glance.leader: Xi Jinping; Wang Yi carries the foreign file with delegated authority
glance.gdp: About $20.9tn nominal (IMF, 2026); 4.7% growth in the first half against a 4.5-5% target, July exports up 23.9% year on year
glance.military: About 2.0 million active, the largest standing force in the world; announced defence budget in the $280bn range
glance.influence: Buyer of last resort for sanctioned barrels, rare earths and the export machine, coast-guard jurisdiction pressure around Taiwan and the East China Sea, and a summit Washington wants

dossiers.summary: Beijing's constraint this quarter is the calendar, not the doctrine. A state visit on 24 September and a tariff truce expiring in November are both worth more than any concession on Iranian crude, which is why the buying continues while the rhetoric stays defiant - and why Treasury sanctioned an Egyptian bank's UAE branches rather than a Chinese one. An enforcer that keeps picking the cheapest nail is telling you which nail is expensive. The desk to watch is not the foreign ministry but the coast guard and the customs administration: PLA sorties around Taiwan have been declining while jurisdictional assertion has been rising, and that ratchet - salami tactics in Schelling's sense, slices too thin to fight over individually - is the actual instrument. Read the summit as accumulation under cover of detente rather than as a thaw, and keep the discount small: announced head-of-state visits with active staff preparation happen about 90% of the time. The tell that breaks the benign read is a coast-guard action inside the visit window; the tell that breaks the leverage read is a blocking designation on a top-ten Chinese bank before 24 September.

concerns: Coast-guard normalization and seabed mapping are precondition-building around Taiwan, not the event itself
China is the load-bearing leak in the Iran sanctions siege - Mulder's rule is that a siege is only as tight as its leakage path
The tariff truce expires in November, just after the summit, which is where a cheap concession becomes an expensive one
A defiant public line paired with quiet compliance makes intent unreadable from statements; only flows settle it

dossiers.name: Israel

glance.government: Parliamentary democracy; the Knesset dissolved in July and the election is set for 27 October 2026
glance.leader: Benjamin Netanyahu, prime minister; Israel Katz defence minister and the cabinet's designated hawk
glance.gdp: About $720bn nominal on 2026 estimates, with defence spending near 8% of GDP
glance.influence: Air superiority over the Levant, the Washington relationship, and an undeclared nuclear status the state has never confirmed

dossiers.summary: Read every Israeli decision for the next seven weeks through 27 October. That is the constraint, and it is a calendar rather than a character: a prime minister facing an election needs deliverables that are visible, mapped and finished, which is exactly what a declared security zone is. On 4 September Katz said the capture of the Ali al-Taher ridge completes the phase of securing control in southern Lebanon and that there will be no withdrawal until Hezbollah is disarmed throughout the country - a condition the Lebanese state has never been able to meet, which makes the presence open-ended by construction. The desk that decides is not the cabinet podium but Northern Command's force-generation math and the finance ministry's reserve-duty bill, because holding ground costs manpower in a way air power does not. Note also the direction this cuts: history says a held buffer produces chronic attrition rather than episodic campaigns, which is why this board CUT its multi-week-campaign odds on the day the zone was declared. Separately, national security minister Ben Gvir published a twenty-page plan for what he calls voluntary emigration of Gaza's population - 250,000 in the first year and the remainder over six more. It is a minister's document rather than cabinet policy, and forced transfer of civilians from occupied territory is a war crime under the Geneva Conventions; it is logged here as a coalition signal, not as a programme.

concerns: The 27 October election makes restraint politically expensive at exactly the wrong moment
A withdrawal condition the Lebanese state cannot satisfy converts an operation into an occupation by definition
The Lebanon framework still has no third-party verifier and the party being disarmed rejects the premise
Ministerial transfer plans for Gaza, even unimplemented, carry legal and coalition exposure that outlasts the cabinet

dossiers.name: Germany

glance.government: Federal parliamentary republic; coalition government under a chancellor with weak approval numbers
glance.leader: Friedrich Merz, chancellor; Alexander Dobrindt at the Interior Ministry carries the attribution and the police file, which is why the response is expulsions rather than an alliance consultation
glance.gdp: Roughly $4.9tn nominal - unverified against a current print; the binding number this quarter is energy input cost rather than headline output
glance.military: About 182,000 active on standard counts, with a rearmament programme running against recruitment shortfalls; unverified against a current IISS figure
glance.influence: Europe's largest industrial gas consumer, the logistics bridge to Ukraine through Leipzig/Halle, and the swing vote on every EU sanctions and energy instrument

dossiers.summary: Germany's constraint is a vice with an energy jaw and a security jaw, and both tightened this week. It replaced Russian pipeline gas with seaborne LNG, which traded a political dependency for a maritime one - so a war at Hormuz now reaches German industry directly, with continental storage near 62 percent against a seasonal norm around 79. At the same time it is the physical bridge over which munitions reach Ukraine, which is precisely why an explosive drone came down at Leipzig/Halle rather than at a barracks. Read the response for what it reveals about the ceiling: the desk that acted was the Interior Ministry, and the instruments were a consulate closure, a cultural-institute contract and visa tightening - the diplomatic rail, chosen because it is cheap, reversible and does not require asking twenty-six other governments for permission. The official story is resolve; the incentive read is a chancellor with poor ratings who gains from a clear adversary, which is a reason to scrutinise the timing rather than to assume it.

concerns: Gas storage near 62 percent with winter arriving is an industrial-cost problem before it is a household one, and German industry is the marginal European buyer
A sabotage campaign aimed at logistics rather than forces sits deliberately below any alliance threshold - which is what makes it repeatable
The attribution was published without forensics or charges, so its political durability depends on evidence Berlin has not yet shown
Moscow has promised to mirror the expulsions, which costs Germany intelligence access it may value more than the consulate it closed

dossiers.name: United States

glance.government: Federal presidential republic; midterm elections 3 November 2026
glance.leader: Donald Trump; Scott Bessent at Treasury, Marco Rubio at State, Pete Hegseth at Defense, Kevin Warsh at the Federal Reserve
glance.gdp: Roughly $30tn nominal on standard 2026 estimates - unverified against a current print; federal debt past $40tn
glance.military: About 1.34 million active with roughly 770,000 reserve and National Guard; budget in the $900bn range
glance.influence: Dollar clearing and OFAC designations, CENTCOM escort of the strait, and a rate path that prices everyone else's oil bill

dossiers.summary: The American constraint hardened today and it is arithmetic rather than politics. August payrolls came in at 162,000 against a 53,000 consensus with unemployment at 4.1%, which removes the soft-landing argument for cutting; simultaneously diesel set an all-time record at $5.820 a gallon on a refining shortage no interest rate can fix. That is the RESCUE WITHHELD configuration - a market pricing help in a shock where help does not exist - and the long end already agrees, with the ten-year at 4.79% and the thirty-year at 5.27%, both above this board's published red lines, and the reverse-repo buffer down to $0.70bn. The desk that decides is not the podium: it is the FOMC, the refiners' turnaround calendar and the weekly EIA distillate print, in that order of who can actually change the number. Foreign policy is being run on the same logic - allies invoiced for contributions at Hormuz, a Venezuelan venture organised around one man's legal exposure rather than around built infrastructure, and a president who declined this week to say whether the United States would defend Britain in another Falklands war. Each of those is leverage bought cheaply now against a commitment payable later.

concerns: Record diesel is the invisible half of the inflation problem, because it prices freight, farming and heating rather than only the pump
A hot labour print into a hiking debate removes the monetary rescue markets keep assuming
Enforcement at Hormuz is now a standing commitment - a lane you must keep clearing is not a victory
Alliance ambiguity is being used as leverage in three theatres at once, and credibility spent in one is not recoverable in another
Confirmed American casualties would collapse the intercepted-volley equilibrium the whole restraint posture rests on

dossiers.name: Japan

glance.government: Constitutional monarchy with a parliamentary system; Bank of Japan policy decision due 18 September 2026
glance.leader: Emperor Naruhito as head of state; the Bank of Japan governorship is the office that matters for this file - the policy board, not the cabinet, sets the variable the world is watching
glance.gdp: Roughly $4.2tn nominal on standard 2026 estimates - unverified against a current print; policy rate 0.75 per cent, a thirty-year high, with ten-year government bond yields near 3 per cent for the first time since 1996
glance.military: Self-Defense Forces of about 247,000 active personnel; defence spending on a path toward 2 per cent of GDP
glance.influence: The world's cheap funding currency, one of the largest foreign holders of US Treasuries, and a carry trade estimated anywhere between $500bn and over $4tn depending on definition

dossiers.summary: Japan appears on this board for a plumbing reason rather than a diplomatic one, and it is the reason the board opened a new forecast today. For thirty years Japan supplied the world with money that cost nothing - zero rates from 1999, then quantitative and qualitative easing from 2013 - and the world spent it on everything from Mexican bonds to American technology. That arrangement is now unwinding, not because Tokyo chose a new geopolitics but because Japan finally has inflation, imported partly through a weak yen and partly through an energy bill that this year's Hormuz disruption has made worse. The constraint on the policy board is therefore domestic and blunt: households are angry about food and fuel prices, exporters and the equity index need the weak currency, and every previous attempt to tighten has met that second constituency and delivered less than markets priced. The desk that decides is the BoJ policy board on 18 September; the desk that transmits is the leveraged fund complex and the Japanese insurers and pension funds holding vast foreign bond portfolios. Watch the yen rather than the statement - a hike with the currency through 150 is the confirmation leg, and a hike with the yen drifting back above 160 is another false start in a long series.

concerns: A disorderly carry unwind transmits a Tokyo rate decision into global asset prices within hours, as it did in August 2024
The size of the borrowed-yen stack is genuinely unknown - published estimates span an order of magnitude
Higher domestic yields give Japanese institutions a reason to repatriate from Treasuries exactly as US issuance runs heaviest
Imported energy costs are the transmission line from the Strait of Hormuz into Japanese inflation and therefore into this policy decision

scenarios.q: What if the Iran exchange breaks its interception equilibrium?
scenarios.read: Four nights of strikes have produced no American death and no struck US hull, and that is not restraint - it is arithmetic. Iran fires target-matched volleys at hardened bases, air defences intercept most of them, and both governments get to claim a result. The fire has now landed on six host states, and each new launch site and host country adds draws from the same distribution. Equilibria of this kind fail at their widest edge, not their centre.

stages.s: Within 14 days: a further multi-night exchange with leakers - damage or casualties on a host-state base, even without American deaths. Falsifier: a fortnight of quiet, or Muscat publishing corridor coordinates.

Within 30 days: a confirmed American death or a struck US-flagged hull - the published CRITICAL trigger on this board. Falsifier: the trigger unfired on 3 October, which we will log as scored rather than deferred.
Within 60 days of such an event: a sustained multi-week campaign against Iranian state targets, which is what GEO-003 resolves on at 43 per cent.
Beyond: a Gulf host state publicly withdraws basing consent or restricts US operations from its soil - the newly armed wire, and the sequel nobody prices. Most branches die at stage A.

scenarios.falsifier: Fourteen days with no further exchange and a published minesweeping calendar out of Muscat kills this branch, sends GEO-003 back to about 31 and GEO-001 back toward 21 - scored as a miss, not deferred.

scenarios.q: What if the yen carry unwind arrives before the Bank of Japan wants it?
scenarios.read: The mechanism is a funding leg, not a currency view. For thirty years the yen has been the cheapest money in the world, borrowed to buy higher-yielding assets everywhere else; a rising yen raises the cost of the loan and cuts the value of the collateral at the same moment, which forces selling of the good assets rather than the bad ones. That is why August 2024 transmitted a Tokyo rate decision into a global drawdown inside a day. The published estimates of the stack span an order of magnitude, which is itself the risk - nobody can size the thing that would be unwinding.

stages.s: Within 30 days: the BoJ hikes on 18 September and USD/JPY breaks 150 - the armed tripwire and the confirmation leg. Falsifier: a hold, or a hike with guidance that it is the last one, and the yen back above 160.

Within 90 days: an 8 per cent yen appreciation inside a rolling 30-day window, which is what GEO-025 resolves on at 28 per cent, accompanied by visible drawdowns in the assets bought with borrowed yen. Falsifier: the yen appreciating in an orderly grind with equity volatility unchanged.

Within 6 months: coordinated intervention or an emergency BoJ statement on the long end, or a Japanese institutional repatriation visible in Treasury holdings data. Falsifier: TIC data showing Japanese holdings flat.
Beyond: a funding event rather than a price event - a dealer or fund failure attributed to yen-denominated leverage. Most branches die at stage A and this one is designed to.

scenarios.falsifier: A hold on 18 September with USD/JPY back above 160 by mid-October kills this branch and scores the front-running read a miss. Japan has signalled tightening and under-delivered repeatedly, and that is the base case this branch has to beat.

scenarios.q: What if the diesel squeeze outlasts the war that caused it?
scenarios.read: The mechanism is capital stock, not conflict. Crude supply responds to price in weeks because valves open; refining supply responds in years because units get built, and nobody builds a hydrocracker on a two-year price signal in a decarbonising policy environment. So the interesting question is not whether the shooting stops - it is whether, when it does, the world discovers it had been running on refining slack that no longer exists. Three pulls are live at once: Gulf product flows through a contested strait, Russian refineries under drone attack with an export ban to 30 September, and Western turnaround intervals stretched past prudence. Any one of them ending is a headline. All three would have to end for the crack to normalise, and only one of them has a published expiry date.

stages.s: Within 30 days: the crack stays above $70 and at least one government moves from complaint to allocation - an export restriction floated, a strategic reserve release of distillate, or a farm-diesel subsidy. Falsifier: the crack settles under $45 and this branch dies here, which is exactly what GEO-026 is written to score.

Within 90 days: heating-season demand meets record-low East Coast stocks and diesel becomes an explicitly political price in the US midterm campaign, the way petrol was in 2022. Falsifier: East Coast distillate rebuilds above 30 million barrels before 1 December.

Within 6 months: refining margin becomes a stated object of policy - windfall levies, mandated domestic supply obligations, or a state-backed refinery investment programme in a G7 country. Falsifier: no G7 legislature tables a refining-specific measure.

Beyond: the least substitutable step in the oil chain is permanently outside the West - Jamnagar, Ruwais, Dangote and Chinese teapots setting the world diesel price the way Rotterdam once did. Most branches die at stage A or B and this one is built to.

scenarios.falsifier: A US diesel crack settling below $45 a barrel before 15 December with the strait still contested kills this branch outright and scores the outage read - and we publish that as a miss rather than as not yet.

scenarios.q: What if the Pentagon's Venezuelan stake becomes fixed infrastructure?
scenarios.read: The mechanism is Churchill's, not anyone's from this decade: a state that cannot guarantee its fuel with geology buys the producer instead - the Royal Navy took 51 per cent of Anglo-Persian in June 1914 for exactly this reason. What separates a supply rail from a fee extracted from a client government is logistics. Orinoco extra-heavy crude is near-solid at reservoir temperature and needs diluent, upgraders, power and channel depth; equity does not move a barrel, dredging does.

stages.s: Within 30 days: a published contract text with a governing law, an arbitration seat and a named sanctions authorisation. Falsifier: the 8 September signing session passes with no instrument published.

Within 6 months: an Office of Strategic Capital loan or guarantee facility announced against Venezuelan production. Chevron's $7bn moves this stage but does not resolve it. Falsifier: no facility named and Exxon still absent.

Within 18 months: an awarded, funded dredging contract or a dedicated heavy-crude terminal tender - the GEO-022 resolution and the premeditation tell. Falsifier: equity and capex in place, no logistics award.
Beyond: US Gulf heavy sourcing measurably swings off the Middle East and the Canadian heavy discount widens. Most branches die at stage A and this one is designed to.

scenarios.falsifier: Eighteen months with the stake in place and no funded logistics award means this was spoils rather than a pre-built rail, and we score the premeditation read a miss rather than deferring it.

chatter.claim: That both of the world's oil chokepoints are already closed and the shortage is being managed rather than reported - the standing war general opens each thread with the line Hormuz and Bab el Mandeb Strait Status: Closed, and an energy-emergency entry saying the IEA is warning of a global oil shortage as global and US strategic petroleum reserves run out.
chatter.spread: The /ww3g/ WW3 General on /pol/, now at day 189 and reposted every few hours with a fixed status header, cross-posted into /pig/ at over 260 replies.
chatter.read: Maps onto the managed-scarcity frame, and its kernel is unusually strong: Hormuz has been effectively shut since March, the Red Sea is genuinely the substitute route, and reserve drawdowns are published fact. The failure is in the binary. Bab al-Mandab transits were RISING as recently as the 17-23 August week, which a status line cannot express. easy.bottomLine: The biggest thing today is a fight over a doorway. Most of the world's oil used to leave the Middle East through one narrow strait called Hormuz, but that has been shut since March, so Saudi Arabia started pumping its oil across the country through a pipeline and sending it out the other side, through a second narrow doorway at the bottom of the Red Sea called Bab al-Mandab. On Thursday the Houthis, a group in Yemen, attacked toward that second doorway with rockets, drones and soldiers on the ground. By Friday 129 people had been killed - the worst fighting in Yemen in years. Here is the part most people are getting wrong: ships are still going through. The people who insure ships have decided the Houthis are only attacking Saudi ships, not everyone's, so the rest of the world is still sailing. That makes this a squeeze on one country rather than a closed door - for now.
easy.risk: Still HIGH, and for the same reason as the rest of this week: our own rule says it only goes to the very top step if an American is killed or an American ship is hit, and neither happened. Three different countries were pressured today in three different ways - a rifle in Yemen, a threat aimed at Iran, and a bank punished in Turkey - and none of them crossed our line. The thing to keep watching is not the number of people killed in Yemen. It is how many ships go through that doorway each day.
easy.markets: Strong jobs news is bad news for anyone with a loan. America added 162,000 jobs in August when experts expected about 58,000, and unemployment stayed at 4.1 per cent. A strong jobs market means the Federal Reserve is more likely to RAISE interest rates rather than cut them, so borrowing gets more expensive - and share prices dipped on the news. The next big number is the inflation report on 11 September, and the Fed decides on the 16th. Meanwhile every barrel of oil that has to take the long way round adds about $2.6 million in extra fuel and canal fees per trip, and that ends up in the price of diesel.
brief: A group in Yemen called the Houthis attacked toward the narrow sea gate at the bottom of the Red Sea, and 129 people were killed in two days. It matters because Saudi Arabia started sending its oil that way after the other big sea gate closed, so the Houthis are attacking the backup route rather than the main one.

President Trump said America may soon bomb an Iranian site called Pickaxe Mountain - a set of tunnels dug about 100 metres under a mountain. Nuclear inspectors have been banned from Iran since the fighting started, so nobody outside Iran actually knows for sure what is inside; the threat itself makes Iran spend money moving things around.

The head of Homeland Security said states must let his department look at their voting machines and voter lists, or officials could be fined or jailed. His letter to Nevada said up to 15,903 non-citizens might be registered to vote - but when his own staff checked them one by one, they confirmed 185. Running elections is a state job, not a federal one, so this is pressure rather than law.

America punished a small bank in Turkey, saying it helped Iran turn oil money sitting in China into cash and gold. The point is not the oil - Iran can still sell it. The point is that Iran struggles to turn that money into money it can actually spend, and America controls the pipes most banks use to move dollars.

The United Nations voted 164 to 1 to stop using the old world map, the one that makes Africa look small and Greenland look huge, and use a fairer one instead. It does not force anyone to do anything - the real decision belongs to the companies that make the maps on your phone. America cast the only vote against.

risk.line: Still HIGH, and held there by the published rule rather than by the day's volume: the top step needs a confirmed American death or a struck US-flagged hull, and neither happened. What did happen is that the world's substitute route came under ground attack. Since the Strait of Hormuz closed in March, Saudi Arabia has been pushing crude across the East-West pipeline to Yanbu and out through the Red Sea, and Kpler-tracked volumes through Bab al-Mandab rose roughly eightfold; on Thursday the Houthis opened a ground offensive with rockets and drones toward Mokha and the high ground above the strait, and by Friday an AFP tally of military sources put the dead at 129 - Yemen's worst fighting in years. Read the number that spoils the neat story before the ones that confirm it: the Joint Maritime Information Center recorded at least 302 transits through the same chokepoint between 17 and 23 August, the highest since the Saudi ban, because underwriters have concluded the threat is aimed at a specific subset of Saudi-linked tonnage rather than at shipping generally. So the correct reading today is a DISCRIMINATING blockade, not a closed gate - dangerous precisely because it is cheap to sustain and hard to internationalise. Alongside it, Trump said from the White House that the US may hit Iran's Pickaxe Mountain very soon, the buried tunnel complex near Natanz that the June 2025 strikes pointedly skipped; that is a sentence, not an operation, and the observable that converts it is bomber movement, not rhetoric. Treasury designated a small Istanbul bank as an Iranian conversion channel the same afternoon. Three theatres, one instrument each - a rifle, a threat and a designation - and none of them tripped our own escalation rule.

forecasts.q: Brent stays inside the $80-100 band

The wording is restated for the third session because it decides the score: $99.38 was an INTRADAY print and this question resolves on DAILY CLOSES, so nothing has breached. Still the closest call on the board and our first Brier score.

Reiter is the anchor - wars end when belligerents' expectations converge, and shuttle diplomacy is a symptom of convergence rather than a cause of it. Katz declared the south Lebanon security zone complete and conditioned withdrawal on Hezbollah being disarmed throughout Lebanon. A HELD BUFFER is historically a SUBSTITUTE for episodic campaigns rather than a prelude to them: the 1985-2000 security zone produced continuous low-grade attrition punctuated by roughly two multi-week operations in fifteen years - Accountability in 1993, Grapes of Wrath in 1996 - a class base rate near 13% a year against the 32% carried here. Fortna is what keeps the number well ABOVE that historical rate rather than at it: this framework has no third-party verifier and the party being disarmed rejects the premise. Falsifier for the cut: an Israeli air campaign north of the Litani lasting more than a week would show consolidation was a launchpad, and we were wrong to trim.

forecasts.q: NEW - US diesel crack spread settles back below $45/bbl on any day before 15 Dec 2026
forecasts.note: OPENED at 35, paying the largest unwritten plumbing debt on this board. The prints that force it: the US diesel crack made an all-time intraday high of $108.02 on Wednesday and last traded near $101, the national average diesel price hit a record $5.820 a gallon beating June 2022, East Coast distillate stocks are at a record-low 19.3 million barrels, and August national distillate stocks were the lowest for the month since 1982. Written deliberately on the MEAN-REVERSION side so that our house lean - that this is a regime rather than an outage - is the side that has to be proven. Base rate first: outage-driven product-crack spikes revert inside three to six months, and the May 2022 diesel spike was back under $45 by that August, which argues near 45 over a fourteen-week window. Adjusted DOWN to 35 because three causes run at once rather than one - roughly 900,000 b/d of diesel and 350,000 b/d of jet normally leave the Gulf through a contested strait, Russia has banned diesel exports to 30 September after Ukrainian drone strikes on its refineries, and US refiners are running stretched turnaround intervals - and because the heating season and the autumn harvest are both still ahead of the demand curve rather than behind it.

forecasts.q: NEW - US publicly departs from formal neutrality on Falklands sovereignty before 31 Mar 2027
forecasts.note: OPENED at 12, paying a Latin America coverage debt on the day the question became live. It resolves on a State Department or White House STATEMENT endorsing negotiation over sovereignty or recognising the Argentine claim - a document, not an interview answer. The base rate is the anchor and it is brutal: no US administration has moved off the 1982 formulation in forty-four years, sovereignty transfers of inhabited territory against the inhabitants' expressed wishes essentially do not occur in the post-1945 order outside decolonization or war, and the 2013 referendum ran 99.8% to remain British. Adjusted up from about 5 on named evidence: Trump declined on camera to say the US would come to Britain's aid, said on Monday that he always reviews every position, and Milei responded within hours with a national address, an urgent sovereignty bill and penalties aimed at the Sea Lion project's shareholders, directors and suppliers. The boring alternative is named explicitly and is the leading one - a president answers a hypothetical expansively, State never changes a word, and this is a news cycle.

hypotheses.name: IRGC captured the succession (weak form — assessed finding)
hypotheses.d: Documented pressure on Assembly electors, 8 boycotts, overridden shortlist and will. The pre-arranged-pact version scores only 30% — the plan was overridden, not executed.

hypotheses.name: The IRGC, not Mojtaba, rules Iran (working model) — HELD 82%
hypotheses.d: HELD. The promised authenticated footage of Mojtaba meeting commanders still has not landed, so the falsifier remains un-run. The week was IRGC-forward — the Guard, not the foreign ministry, confirmed it ran the Oman channel and announced the revenue-sharing terms, and the Guard made the mine-strike claim — but that is DENIED as a raise under the shared-prediction rule: 'the Guard runs the maritime file' is predicted just as strongly by an ordinary reading in which the IRGC is a powerful institution under a functioning Supreme Leader, which is a much weaker claim than 'the IRGC rules Iran'. The 82% cap stands for exactly the reason it was set.

hypotheses.name: The Iran file is coalition-captured (the capture read, tracked as opinion)
hypotheses.d: The claim: on the Iran file, organized coalition pressure — donor networks, primary structure, allied commitments, defense-institutional momentum — outweighs the base's war fatigue, which is why a 'no more wars' White House struck anyway and now substitutes sanctions for settlement rather than sign a visible retreat before the midterms. Mechanisms named, plural: status clock vs electoral clock, sunk cost after declaring victory, lobbies as veto players that raise the price of defection (one interest group among several — any single-key version of this hypothesis is scored separately and currently rejected). Held at 70%: the strike itself, the 6-month grind, and 'not in a hurry' all fit; capped because the same facts also fit ordinary planning failure plus vanity. Falsifier: a signed de-escalation or negotiated Hormuz reopening BEFORE the midterms — the base's clock winning on the party's most captured file would kill the strong form outright.

hypotheses.name: Nobody's hurrying on Hormuz — 60% → 65% (RAISED)
hypotheses.d: Its first fact that BEATS a rival instead of merely fitting itself. On 30 Aug the US struck two IRGC rocket launchers on Larak after observing Guard personnel preparing to fire rockets carrying sea mines into the strait — two days after CENTCOM declared the lanes fully cleared, and while Muscat negotiates a minesweeping calendar. The 08-30 audit had installed a genuine rival — a physical clock, minesweeping simply takes time — and ruled this hypothesis must beat it. A physical clock runs down; this one is being rewound, by the exact actor the hypothesis named in advance. Capped at +5 on three counts kept in front: CENTCOM is the interested party and 'observed preparations' is unpublished intelligence used to justify a strike; Al Jazeera published a technical challenge on 31 Aug to whether Iran can even mine by rocket as claimed; and IRGC counter-coercion against a blockade that has redirected 83 vessels, disabled three and boarded two explains the same act without any rent motive. Not pre-event.

hypotheses.name: Détente as harvest cover — HELD 60%, tell sharpened
hypotheses.d: August continues the signature: 125 PLA aerial ADIZ incursions (the 2026 decline intact) against 152 non-warship PRC vessels in the first 21 days, ~60% coast guard, with the east-of-Taiwan patrols now a declared 'new normal'. Kinetic down, jurisdiction up. NOT moved — this is the same signal that bought +5 on 08-26, and re-marking on the continuation of its own evidence is the double-count the audit named. The important item is against my own test: if Beijing has DECLARED the patrols permanent, their persistence through the Sept 24 visit is close to uninformative. Re-specified now, in advance and stricter — the informative observation on 09-23→09-25 is a boarding, an inspection, or a first-time-area incursion. Mere presence no longer counts as confirmation.

hypotheses.name: Venezuela was a Hormuz hedge in a drug-war uniform
hypotheses.d: The clearest revealed-preference play on the board — and the reason it holds at 55 rather than higher. Sturdy mechanism first: US Gulf-Coast refineries are plumbed for heavy sour crude, Venezuela sits on the planet's largest heavy reserves, and moving that barrel north through the Caribbean to Texas and Louisiana structurally hedges the one risk that ran live all year — a Hormuz closure. The Aug 28-29 deal (a new operator taking control of ~65bn barrels, about a fifth of Venezuela's reserves) is exactly what this hypothesis predicts. So oil-as-motive is near-certain. What is NOT settled — and what caps this — is premeditation: was Southern Spear a counter-narcotics and regime-change campaign that harvested the oil after the fact, or an oil-security operation in a drug-war uniform from the start? The tell against design is the clock — the deal trailed Maduro's Jan 3 capture by eight months, which reads more like spoils than master plan. Falsifiers: token export volumes, Gulf-Coast heavy sourcing not actually swinging off the Middle East, or the fixed infrastructure (GEO-022) never appearing. One correction the excitement needs: a canal cannot bypass Hormuz — the hedge is source substitution plus Caribbean routing, not a waterway. Note it is DISTINCT from 'The Portfolio State' below, which is about the vehicle rather than the motive.

hypotheses.name: US drift hardened into leverage play — HELD 52%
hypotheses.d: Confirming but shared, therefore ambience: Treasury again held back on Chinese financial institutions, with mainstream reporting now naming the mechanism outright — designating them 'could create tensions before Xi's visit'. Bessent's promised weekly cadence hit banks but no Chinese one, and at the G20 he pushed severing Iran financial ties while China dissented. Both the leverage read and the ordinary 'Washington won't detonate its own summit' read predict all of it. The strongest weekly argument AGAINST, logged rather than absorbed: the US struck Iran on three consecutive nights and took Iranian fire onto three Arab host states. Deliberate slow-walking for leverage sits badly with sustained kinetic escalation that raises the cost of the thing being slow-walked — that counterweight is what holds the number at 52.

hypotheses.name: A pre-announcement leak into oil futures — 40% → 34% (biggest mover)
hypotheses.d: Its lead conditional has now gone unfired across three weeks containing the most violently market-moving Iran news since April — the 30 Aug Larak strike, three nights of exchanges, two struck VLCCs, Brent to ~$95 — with not one reported nine-figure pre-announcement episode. The file is confirmed as historical and bounded: DOJ is probing four trades totalling ~$2.6bn, all inside a five-week window that closed in April — Mar 23 (>$500m, ~15 min before Trump's delay post), Apr 7 ($960m before the ceasefire), Apr 17 ($760m, ~20 min before Iran said Hormuz was open), Apr 21 ($430m before the extension). CORRECTION BANKED AGAINST THIS ENTRY: the ledger's earlier '~$2.2bn cluster' for Mar 23 and its '~$7bn' aggregate are both withdrawn as over-wide constructions. The cut is made on the hypothesis's own written terms, not on a preferred reading — a conditional set at 60% has burned three of fourteen weeks in the best environment it will ever get and produced nothing. The cut is only −6 because of one genuinely new structural fact: investigators are running a SEPARATE probe into prediction-market activity on the same developments, and the same foreknowledge reaching two unrelated venues is hard to explain as one market-maker hedging client flow. Split now: deliberate leak 34 / mediator-side 20 / skilled opportunism 36 / coincidence 10. Still the only entry whose evidence is timestamped BEFORE the event.

hypotheses.name: NEW · The Portfolio State — coercion converted into sovereign equity, statute retrofitted
hypotheses.d: Strongest form: the US is converting military and sanctions leverage into permanent state equity in strategic supply chains, with the legal authority written to fit transactions rather than the reverse — Venezuela being the first hydrocarbon use of a template already run in chips and critical minerals. The rail predates the headline, which is the only thing licensing a design read at all: Senate NDAA FY2027 §1051 was marked up in MID-JUNE — ten weeks before the 29 Aug deal — creating a DoD Equity Investment Account, authorising OSC equity to $500m and capping any single position at 40% of the entity; the Venezuela stake is 35%, inside a cap that does not legally exist yet. Add DoD's own $400m/15% stake in MP Materials with 100% offtake (structurally identical to Venezuela's '20% of output at cost'), House Oversight already demanding an accounting of Venezuelan oil revenue on 23 Feb, and CFR's tally of 26 government equity deals worth ~$23.9bn. It opens at only 25% because the boring, incompetence and patronage readings are all strong: think tanks have been publicly naming and counting this pattern since 2025 (a policy, not a plot); the Pentagon's own spokesman flatly DENIES that OSC takes equity while WSJ reports it doing so, which is improvisation not design; and a 100-year concession over 65bn bbl routed to one politically connected operator with no published contract is better explained as spoils allocation. Above all the base rate is enormous — Anglo-Persian 1914, the RFC, GM/Chrysler 2009 — so the design premium must be small. NOT a conspiracy claim and must never be scored as one: it requires no secrecy at all, only anticipation, and the honest gap is that I cannot name the operator who executes the warrants. Key test: does the ENACTED NDAA widen §1051 beyond critical minerals to energy, or raise the cap, by 31 Dec (45%)? Scope enacted unchanged kills the design read.

hypotheses.name: Moscow shapes Tehran's maximalism — 25% → 22% (CUT, sixth session running)
hypotheses.d: The week finally produced Russia-Iran material and it is the wrong KIND. Moscow said publicly on 01 Sep that air defence is the main focus of military-technical cooperation with Iran, alongside a reported 500 Verba MANPADS and 2,500 missiles and continued fighter deliveries. That is the resupply leg — already priced at 7/10 under 'means'. It moves nothing: it is announced by TASS, an interested party publishing its own helpfulness and the structural opposite of a covert channel; the opportunism branch predicts arms sales to a client at war identically, so under the standing rule it is ambience; and after six sessions there is still ZERO documentary evidence Moscow has influenced Tehran's negotiating position, which is the actual claim. Arms transfers are not persuasion. Cut rather than held because a decay rule that bites only on its deadline is a cliff, not decay. Clock unchanged: 15% on 30 Sep absent documentary evidence, retire below 10%.

hypotheses.name: War pause was secretly packaged with the Beijing summit — on the retirement line
hypotheses.d: Nothing resolved this week, and one file addition cuts against it: the summit's Iran content is now openly reported as an explicit US ask — Chinese pressure on Tehran to reopen the strait — with Beijing expected to want Taiwan concessions in return. An openly negotiated Iran-for-Taiwan trade is this hypothesis's RIVAL, not its confirmation; the secret-package version needs the deal hidden, and the deal is being conducted in headlines. Retirement trigger unchanged; the test runs on schedule on 24 Sept.

brief.head: Houthis storm toward Bab al-Mandab in Yemen's deadliest fighting in years
brief.h: A Houthi ground assault backed by rockets and drones opened on Thursday against Mokha and the high ground above the Red Sea's southern gate, and by Friday an AFP tally from military sources put the dead at 129 - 39 government fighters, 24 of them on the coast and 15 around Taiz, against at least 42 Houthi dead - with the rebels holding elevated sites overlooking government positions.
brief.t: The target is not Yemen, it is the detour. When Hormuz closed in March the world did not stop moving oil; it re-plumbed, and Saudi Arabia pushed crude across the East-West pipeline to Yanbu and out through the Red Sea, with Kpler-tracked volumes through Bab al-Mandab rising roughly eightfold. Attacking the strait now is therefore not a second front - it is an attack on the WORKAROUND, and that is the whole design: you do not have to close a chokepoint if you can make the alternative to it expensive. Price the mechanism rather than the map. A cargo forced off a VLCC onto a Suezmax carries half the barrels and adds around $1.6m in fuel plus a $1m Suez toll per transit, so every mile of re-routing is a tax collected by geography and paid at a refinery gate. Then say the thing that spoils the story: transits are UP. The Joint Maritime Information Center logged at least 302 hulls through the strait between 17 and 23 August, the highest since the Saudi ban, because the market has concluded the threat is aimed at a specific subset of Saudi-linked tonnage. What is being run is a DISCRIMINATING blockade - cheap to sustain, hard to internationalise, and precisely calibrated to stay below the threshold that brings a coalition navy back.
brief.context: R0: the epoch is the post-1967 Suez order, in which Europe's energy and Asia's manufactures were routed through two narrow gates on the assumption that nobody sitting beside them would ever be able to charge for the privilege. The rail predates the headline by a decade - the Houthi coastal missile, drone and uncrewed-boat complex was built through the Saudi war years and demonstrated against shipping from 2023 - so the capability is old and only the target list is new. The constraint on the Houthis is not will but escalation control: hitting Saudi-linked hulls keeps this a Gulf quarrel, while hitting a European boxship or a US-flagged tanker summons the navies that ended the last round. The desk that decides is not Sanaa or Riyadh; it is the war-risk underwriting room at Lloyd's and the JMIC advisory that sets whether a charterer sails, and it prices Saudi tonnage separately from everyone else's. Base rate: ground offensives toward Mokha and the coastal plain have been launched and stalled repeatedly since 2018, when a far larger Emirati-backed force took Hodeidah's outskirts and could not hold the corridor; holding hills above a strait is not the same as closing eighteen miles of water, which requires sustained anti-ship fires and mining. What would change the read is a laden non-Saudi hull hit inside the international lanes - that is the move that converts a discriminating blockade into a closed gate and puts Bab al-Mandab where Hormuz already is.

consp.claim: That both chokepoints are already shut and the public supply picture is being managed rather than reported - the standing WW3 general opens its board with Hormuz and Bab el Mandeb Strait Status: Closed and an energy-emergency line about the IEA warning of shortage as global and US strategic reserves run out, and the Iran thread carries the claim that Iran struck three Saudi tankers trying to bypass what it calls the Persian Gulf Strait Authority.
consp.spread: The /ww3g/ WW3 General on /pol/, now on day 189 and reposted every few hours, alongside /pig/ Persia Israel General at over 260 replies where the tanker and strait claims are tracked as a running scoreboard.
consp.read: The kernel is checkable and largely holds: Hormuz has been effectively closed since March, the Red Sea has become the substitute route, and drawdowns on strategic reserves are real and published. The leap is CLOSED as a binary. Transits through Bab al-Mandab are measurable and were rising as recently as the 17-23 August week, which is exactly the fact a board keeping a scoreboard has no incentive to post. What this is downstream of is genuine information scarcity - when a third of the traffic runs dark and official transit counts lag by days, a status line is easier to believe than a dataset.

angles.effect: convert a coastal missile inventory into a toll on someone else's exports, without owning a port, a tanker or a refinery
pays twice - once for the pipeline detour built to escape Hormuz, and again in war-risk premium on the route that detour leads to
carries it silently: every cargo that skips the Red Sea is a Suez toll not collected, and Cairo has no lever on either belligerent
gets pressure applied to the Saudi export line at arm's length, with no Iranian hull or flag on the invoice
pay the re-routing tax at the pump, which is where a chokepoint fight actually lands

dec.kill: A laden non-Saudi-linked hull struck inside the international lanes, or JMIC transit counts falling materially below the 302-per-week August figure. Mokha holding and transits flat means this was a ground offensive, not a closure.

brief.head: Trump threatens to hit Iran's buried Pickaxe Mountain site soon
brief.h: Speaking to reporters at the White House on Friday, the President said the United States may strike Pickaxe Mountain very soon - the tunnel complex roughly 100 metres under rock beside the damaged Natanz plant, declared to the IAEA in 2021 as a centrifuge assembly hall and assessed by Israeli intelligence to have received centrifuges in autumn 2025 - repeating an earlier formulation that the US would be hitting that area pretty soon, and very heavily, and adding that we follow the material.
brief.t: Three words carry the whole policy: we follow the material. That is a targeting doctrine, and it means the strike list is generated by an intelligence estimate rather than by anything anyone can photograph. Iran is believed to hold close to a thousand pounds of near-weapons-grade uranium; IAEA inspectors have been barred since the strikes began; so the location of the only thing that matters is now an inference held inside two governments. Name the mechanism - TARGETING BY INVENTORY - and its uncomfortable property follows immediately: a strike justified by where the material is assessed to be can never be publicly assessed afterwards, because the same secrecy that authorised it forbids the damage report. Which is why the threat is doing more work unfired than fired. Saying it repeatedly and not acting forces Iran to keep dispersing, moving and re-hardening, and dispersal is expensive, slow and itself a source of the intelligence that generates the next target. Note what the June 2025 strikes did: they hit Fordow, Natanz and Isfahan and pointedly skipped this site. A target left standing for fifteen months and threatened monthly is not an oversight - it is being held.
brief.context: R0: the epoch is the bargain struck at the NPT's founding, in which states accepted inspection in exchange for civil enrichment, and whose enforcement mechanism was always someone else's air force rather than the treaty. The rail predates the headline: the GBU-57 Massive Ordnance Penetrator was commissioned specifically for buried Iranian and North Korean sites, and the B-2 basing at Diego Garcia that makes it deliverable was built for exactly this contingency - the capability is a decade old and the threat is its advertisement. The constraint on Washington is munition inventory and second-order exposure, not appetite: Iran has already answered previous strikes against US bases in Jordan, Bahrain, Erbil and Kuwait, so every deep strike is also a decision to underwrite the hosts. The desk that decides is CENTCOM's targeting cell with the President as release authority; the podium is the instrument, not the decider. Base rate: this specific site has been threatened publicly and repeatedly since July without a strike, so the honest prior on any single threat converting inside a fortnight is low - and the falsifier is physical, not verbal. Bombers arriving at Diego Garcia, a Gulf NOTAM, tanker tracks over the Atlantic: those are what a decision looks like. What would change the read in the other direction is an IAEA re-admission, which would mean the material question is being moved back onto a legal rail.

consp.claim: That American losses in this war are being suppressed - that Iranian missile strikes on US bases in Jordan, Bahrain, Erbil and Kuwait have done far more damage than acknowledged, with a separate thread claiming outright that Iran destroyed an American aircraft carrier.
consp.spread: The /pig/ Persia Israel General on /pol/ at over 260 replies runs this as a scoreboard, and a thread headed ITS FUCKING HAPPENING carried the carrier claim; the counter-argument is being made on the same board, where posters note that not one US ship has been hit in nearly seven months of war.
consp.read: This is the suppressed-losses frame, and its kernel is real: a senior US official's flat denial of any attacks on bases in Jordan is exactly the kind of statement that is sometimes later revised. The leap is from unconfirmed damage to a destroyed capital ship, which is the one claim in the set that cannot survive contact with evidence - a carrier is 5,000 people, a port call and a commercial satellite pass. What is instructive is that the board is policing itself here, and that is the useful signal: when a claim is too big, even a sympathetic audience demands the hull.

angles.effect: gets a coercion instrument that costs nothing until used and imposes real dispersal costs every time it is repeated
pays in movement and hardening rather than in destruction - and keeps the one asset the threat concedes it still has, which is uncertainty about where the material sits
is the quiet loser - a site whose status is settled by bombing is a site whose status is no longer settled by inspection, and the agency has been barred since the strikes began
underwrite the retaliation they did not authorise; their bases are the addresses Iran has already used to answer

dec.kill: Heavy bombers appearing at Diego Garcia on commercial satellite imagery, or a Gulf NOTAM. Three more weeks of the same sentence with no airframe movement means this is a bargaining chip being polished, not a strike being prepared.

brief.head: DHS threatens to prosecute election officials who refuse it access
brief.h: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said foreign adversaries could hack voting machines and promised maximum pressure on states that will not partner with his department, with officials who do not comply facing fines and prison; his letter to Nevada cited as many as 15,903 possible noncitizen registrations, a figure his own officials later called a ceiling in a meeting with the secretary of state's office, against 185 confirmed by manual review.
brief.t: The gap between 15,903 and 185 is not a rounding error, it is the entire method. A database match is a QUESTION - two records that share a name and a birth date - and a confirmation is an ANSWER, and the practice under examination here is publishing the question with the grammar of an answer. Run it against the same office's other numbers and the pattern repeats: 14,576 claimed in Pennsylvania, 8,594 actually matched. Now name the real mechanism, because it is not authority. The Constitution gives the times, places and manner of elections to state legislatures and to Congress, and DHS is neither; courts have repeatedly blocked federal demands for voter rolls. So what is being used instead is leverage - mandatory use of the SAVE immigration database, grant money withheld, and the threat of criminal referral against individual officials. Call it FEDERALISM BY CONDITION: you cannot order a state to hand over a tabulator, but you can make refusing one expensive enough that some state, somewhere, says yes and sets the precedent. The tell that this is not simple partisanship is who refused - Pennsylvania's Republican secretary of state turned it down alongside Nevada's Democrat.
brief.context: R0: the rail is the January 2017 designation of election infrastructure as critical infrastructure, which put a DHS component - now CISA - in an explicitly ADVISORY relationship to state election officials, offering scanning and threat intelligence that states could accept or decline. That advisory rail is what is now being pressed into service as an access demand, which is the classic pattern: the statute is not amended, the posture is. Beneath it sits the Help America Vote Act of 2002 and a federal-state division that has survived every previous federal attempt to centralise voter data, including the 2017 election-integrity commission that collapsed when states refused it. The desk that decides is not the podium and not the department - it is fifty secretaries of state plus the district courts, which is a very large number of veto players for one cabinet officer to move. Base rate is the part the headline needs: the Brennan Center found roughly 30 suspected noncitizen votes among 23.5 million cast in 2016, and the Heritage Foundation's own database records 24 noncitizen cases across twenty years - which makes a claimed 287,000 registrations a statement about database hygiene rather than about votes. What would change the read is a filed criminal charge against a named official, or a court compelling access; either would convert pressure into an instrument.

consp.claim: That the election-access campaign is the wedge for a surveillance architecture already being built - a thread reading a published DHS privacy impact assessment for a Secret Service system called HELIX as the real story, describing continuous biometric, behavioural and digital collection feeding an automated crime coefficient that flags people as latent criminals before an offence, with the voter-roll demand as the entry point for the data.
consp.spread: A /pol/ thread headed HAPPENING with the DHS document linked directly, at around 160 replies, arguing the system is the Sibyl System from Psycho-Pass made operational.
consp.read: The document is real and public, which is why this thread is more interesting than most - a privacy impact assessment is exactly where an agency describes what it intends to collect, and reading one closely is legitimate research rather than invention. The leap is from a records system to precrime, and the anime reference in the thread's own framing is the tell, supplying the ending before the evidence does. The checkable next step is narrow and worth doing: whether the assessment describes behavioural scoring at all, or only record linkage. What this is downstream of is a genuine asymmetry the thread names correctly - the agency knows the scope of its own collection and the public gets a PDF.

angles.effect: acquires a pre-positioned explanation for any midterm result it dislikes, at the cost of nothing that has to survive a court

angles.party: State election officials of both parties
angles.effect: carry personal legal exposure for a federalism dispute they did not start - which is what the threat of fines and prison is for
pay first and quietly, because a database mismatch removes a registration long before a manual review restores it
gain a durable access rail to state voter data that outlasts this election and any particular claim about it

dec.kill: A criminal charge actually filed against a named election official, or any state granting tabulator access. Neither by 3 November means the instrument was pressure rather than policy - and the 185 confirmed against 15,903 claimed stands as the measure of the underlying finding.

brief.head: US sanctions a Turkish bank it calls Iran's financial lifeline
brief.h: Treasury designated Istanbul-based Golden Global Yatirim Bankasi and two subsidiaries for moving tens of millions of dollars for the IRGC's Quds Force and for helping convert Iranian oil revenue held in China into cash and gold in Turkey, the second bank hit under a campaign named Operation Economic Outcast; Scott Bessent said we know who you are, we know where you are - in the same week Halkbank settled a nine-year Justice Department case over roughly $20bn in Iranian oil revenue.
brief.t: The target is not the oil, it is the exit. Iran can still sell barrels - to China, at a discount, in yuan - and that is precisely the problem Tehran has, because a yuan balance sitting in a Chinese account is not spendable on a Russian airframe or a Lebanese payroll. The scarce thing is CONVERSION. So Washington is not trying to stop a cargo; it is trying to strand the proceeds, and the instrument is the correspondent account - the relationship through which a small bank in Istanbul reaches a large bank in New York and therefore reaches the dollar at all. Name it: the DOLLAR CLEARING CHOKEPOINT, the one piece of plumbing that no amount of oil under the ground substitutes for. And read the size of the target as information rather than as weakness. Designating a small investment bank costs Washington nothing diplomatically and teaches every mid-sized institution from Istanbul to Dubai that one Iranian client can cost them the dollar - which is DETERRENCE BY EXAMPLE, executed through compliance departments rather than through courts, and far cheaper than enforcement. The phrase to hold onto is in Treasury's own charge sheet: cash and gold. That is what the flow already looks like when it has been pushed off the wire, and it is the measure of how much of this works.
brief.context: R0: the epoch begins in the 1970s, when the dollar's post-gold role settled onto the plumbing rather than the metal - oil invoiced in dollars, cleared through New York, and therefore visible and interruptible from one desk. The rail long predates this administration: the IEEPA emergency powers, the terrorism and Iran financial-sector executive orders, and the correspondent architecture itself, which was built for settlement efficiency and only later discovered to be a weapon. The constraint on Treasury is credibility rather than reach - each designation spends a little of the assumption that dollar access is a neutral utility, and the second-order effect shows up not in Tehran but in every reserve manager who starts pricing that assumption. The desk that decides is OFAC, not State and not the Pentagon; the operator is the compliance officer at a correspondent bank who quietly declines a relationship nobody ordered him to decline. Base rate: designations of small non-US banks are frequent, rarely reversed, and reliably produce de-risking - the withdrawal of correspondent lines from a whole jurisdiction, which hits banks that never touched an Iranian account. Watch that spillover rather than the designation. What would change the read is evidence the flow simply re-routed into bullion and informal transfer, which the charge sheet arguably already concedes.

consp.claim: That the metal is voting on exactly this - that the Dutch central bank moving roughly 86 tonnes of gold out of New York and Ottawa, after France replaced 129 tonnes held at the New York Fed, is insiders acting on knowledge the public does not have: either that Washington is preparing to restrict or seize foreign holdings, or that the vault cannot deliver what it says it holds.
consp.spread: A /pol/ thread on the Dutch transfer at over 210 replies, running alongside the standing Precious Metals General on /biz/ and posts making the same reading from the Fort Knox audit argument.
consp.read: The kernel is entirely real and confirmed by the central bank itself: DNB moved 86.4 tonnes between March and August and said openly it was preparing for crisis, citing increasing geopolitical unrest, with its London share going from 18.1 to 32.1 per cent. The detail that decides between the two readings is in the mechanics - only about 27 tonnes physically travelled, and the rest was executed as a sale in New York and a purchase in London. A book trade is a LIQUIDITY preference, not a flight from a counterparty you distrust; you cannot sell into a vault you believe is empty. What the frame gets right is the direction: two European central banks have now decided that where your gold sits is a geopolitical variable, and that is new.

angles.effect: gets a cheap, repeatable instrument that works through other people's compliance departments and requires no court
pays in conversion spread rather than in volume - the barrels still sell, the money just costs more to become money
carries the de-risking, which lands hardest on institutions that never had an Iranian client
is handed an argument it has been making for a decade - that dollar clearing is a political instrument - by the act of using it
